Randomisation and masking
Eligible patients were centrally randomly assigned in the
Alea Clinical Portal), in a 1:1:1:1 ratio, to SOC, SOC plus
radiotherapy, SOC plus abiraterone (abiraterone plus
prednisone), or SOC plus radiotherapy plus abiraterone.
This randomisation process was performed via the
Tenalea autonomous software, solely accessed by the trial
data manager within the Epidemioloy and Biostatistics
facility of the Gustave Roussy Center in Villejuif, France
until 2015, then by each investigator.
Randomisation was done using a minimisation
algorithm, stratified by study site, ECOG performance
status (0 vs 1-2), type of ADT (gonadotropin-releasing
hormone agonist vs antagonist vs bilateral orchiectomy),
planned administration of docetaxel (yes vs no), and
disease extent or burden based on metastatic status
(lymph node metastases only vs bone metastases [with or
without lymph node metastases] vs visceral metastases).
A similar weight was given to each of the five
stratification factors, with 80% probability to minimise
imbalance in the number of patients assigned to each
treatment group. As the case report form gathered
information for patient stratification according to
high-volume versus low-volume metastatic burden
classification (as defined in the CHAARTED study2 [high
volume was defined as the presence of visceral
metastases or at least four bone lesions with one beyond
the vertebral bodies and pelvis]), this later classification
was retained to enable inter-trial comparisons. No
masking was performed in this study.
Procedures
In all patients in the study, ADT was planned to be
continuously maintained by either a gonadotropin-
releasing hormone agonist or antagonist, or bilateral
orchiectomy. Patients assigned to receive docetaxel as part
of SOC with continuous ADT were to receive six cycles of
intravenous docetaxel (75 mg/m2 per cycle; maximum
dose of 150 mg per cycle), to be administered every
3 weeks (plus or minus 3 days). Granulocyte colony-
stimulating factor (G-CSF) injections after each docetaxel
cycle were recommended until the protocol amendment
on Jan 22, 2018, made G-CSF prophylaxis mandatory for
patients who received docetaxel. The first docetaxel cycle
had to be administered within 14 days after randomisation
and be at least 6 weeks after ADT initiation. Patients
assigned to receive abiraterone received 1000 mg of
abiraterone (four 250 mg tablets, orally) once daily plus
prednisone 5 mg orally twice daily, starting within 6 weeks
after ADT initiation. PEACE-1 began accrual in 2013,
before the LATITUDE6 and the STAMPEDE7 abiraterone
trials were reported and before abiraterone was approved
for mCSPC, which is why we used 10 mg of prednisone,
similar to what is approved for metastatic castration-
resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC). Abiraterone and
prednisone (hereafter referred to as abiraterone) were
administered until disease progression to castration
resistance, withdrawal of consent, unacceptable toxicity,
or death. Patients assigned to receive radiotherapy
(74 Gy in 37 fractions administered over 7-8 weeks)
were planned to start radiotherapy at least 3 weeks
after docetaxel completion (but no more than 8 weeks
after completion). Treatments given after disease
progression followed common practice, and investigators
were able to change therapy as they thought was most
appropriate, on the basis of prostate-specific antigen
(PSA) concentration variation or clinical progression,
even in absence of radiographical evidence. The treatment
flow chart is depicted in the appendix (p 10).
Every enrolled patient was to be followed-up for a
duration of 10 years. The complete list of assessments
performed at each visit and follow-up intervals are
detailed in the appendix (pp 12-13). Survival status data
were gathered within 3 months of the cutoff date for
97% of patients.
Outcomes
The coprimary endpoints were radiographic progression-
free survival and overall survival. Radiographical pro
gression of soft-tissue lesions was evaluated by either CT
or MRI, on the basis of RECIST version 1.1. Progression
of bone lesions was assessed by bone scan according to
the adapted version of Prostate Cancer Working Group 2
criteria,21 with no secondary bone scan required to
confirm progression. Radiographic progression-free
survival was defined as the time between randomisation
and the occurrence of radiographical progression or
death from any cause. Overall survival was defined as the
time between randomisation and death from any cause.
Patients without events were censored at the date of last
follow-up.
The secondary endpoints were castration-resistant
prostate cancer (CRPC)-free survival, serious-genito
urinary-event-free survival, prostate-cancer-specific survival,
time to next skeletal-related event, PSA response rate,
prognostic study of serum PSA measured 6-8 months
after initiation of systemic therapy, time to pain pro
gression, time to chemotherapy for CRPC, quality of life,
changes in bone mineral density, correlation of biomarkers
with outcome, event rate per 100 person-years of treatment
analysis, and toxicity. CRPC-free survival was defined as
For more on the Alea Clinical
Portal see https://www.
aleaclinical.eu

Institute Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse
Events version 4.0. Safety analysis was based on the highest
grade adverse event recorded during the period spanning
from treatment initiation to CRPC. Apart from CRPC-free
survival, prostate-cancer-specific survival, event rate per
100 person-years, and toxicity, secondary endpoint results
were still under investigation at the time this manuscript
was submitted and so are not reported here.
Statistical analysis
The initial protocol in 2013 planned for a sample size of
916 patients. However, due to a change in the SOC and the
knowledge gained from the LATITUDE and STAMPEDE
trial results published in late 2017, the planned sample
size was increased to 1173 and the coprimary study aims
were revised (appendix pp 7-8). Because PEACE-1 was the
only phase 3 trial to date that could determine abiraterone
efficacy in patients with mCSPC receiving ADT plus
docetaxel as SOC, the timing of the final analyses was
based on this population (population of interest). Sample
size calculation was performed with East software (Cytel;
Cambridge, MA, USA), on the basis of the assumption
that no significant interaction would take place between
radiotherapy and abiraterone, to allow for a 2 × 2 factorial
analysis of abiraterone efficacy. For abiraterone efficacy
evaluation, the predetermined acceptable probability of a
type I error was set at 0·05, divided between the two
coprimary endpoints (0·049 for overall survival and 0·001
for
radiographic
progression-free
survival).
We
hypothesised that adding abiraterone to ADT plus
docetaxel would improve overall survival by 30% over a
median of 53 months and progression-free survival by
40% over 30 months. Hence, with 355 patients assigned to
ADT with docetaxel plus abiraterone (with or without
radiotherapy) and 355 patients assigned to ADT with
docetaxel
without
abiraterone
(with
or
without
radiotherapy), 249 deaths would give an 80% power to
detect an overall survival hazard ratio (HR) of 0·70 at a
two-sided α level of 0·049. With the same group allocation,
262 radiographic progression events or deaths were
predicted to have an 80% power to detect a radiographic
progression-free survival HR of 0·60 at a two-sided α level
of 0·001.
This trial had a factorial design, based on the
assumption that there would be no interaction between
abiraterone and radiotherapy. Before analysing the
various outcomes, the presence of such an interaction
for both coprimary endpoints was tested by analyses of
maximum likelihood estimates using a Cox model
adjusted for stratification factors (ECOG performance
status [0 vs 1-2], ADT type [gonadotropin-releasing
hormone agonist vs antagonist vs bilateral orchiectomy],
metastatic burden [low vs high; as defined in the
Randomisation and masking section],2 and docetaxel
[no docetaxel before amendment vs no docetaxel after
amendment vs with docetaxel after amendment]). In the
absence of a qualitative interaction (p>0·05) between
abiraterone and radiotherapy, the groups were to be
combined two by two on the basis of abiraterone
administration, regardless of radiotherapy, before se
quentially assessing abiraterone efficacy first in the
overall population and then in the ADT with docetaxel
population (assuming the significance level was reached
in first instance). As the preplanned number of pro
gression-free survival and overall survival events had
not been reached in the study population at the time
this paper was written, the efficacy of radiotherapy
remains to be analysed (appendix p 16). The coprimary
endpoint results presented here correspond to the final
planned analysis; no interim analysis was conducted.
All efficacy analyses were conducted in the intention-to-
treat population, defined as all patients who were
randomly assigned to a treatment group. Safety analyses
were conducted in the safety population, according to
the treatment actually received by the patients (those
who did not receive any investigational treatment were
not included in the safety analyses).
The median follow-up was estimated by the inverse
Kaplan-Meier method. Time-to-event endpoints were
estimated by the Kaplan-Meier method. The Cox
proportional hazards model adjusted for radiotherapy
and stratification factors provided significances and an
estimate of the abiraterone effect (p value and HR with
CIs adjusted to match adjustment made to significance
levels in the corresponding test [ie, 99·9% for
radiographic progression-free survival, 95·1% for overall
survival, and 95% for secondary endpoints]). The
assumption of proportional hazards was evaluated on
the basis of the weighted Schoenfeld residuals. The
heterogeneity of the effect of abiraterone in the
predefined stratification subgroups was evaluated using
Cox proportional hazards models adjusted for radio
therapy and stratification factors and including an
interaction term between abiraterone and the studied
stratification variable. These analyses are illustrated
using forest plots. Notably, we analysed the efficacy of
abiraterone in the ADT with docetaxel population by
disease burden. Non-parametric CIs for the median
survival differences between groups were analysed by
the bootkm function of the R Hmisc package

4|Amendments to the study design and statistical analysis plan
5|Since PEACE 1 initial protocol authorization on July 13TH, 2013, the treatment of men with de novo metastatic prostate
6|cancer has drastically evolved. Consequently, the study design and statistical analysis plan had to be adapted accordingly.
7|Changes to the study protocol and statistical analysis plan were made without any reference to the outcomes data collected
8|during the study. All amendments to the protocol were validated by the Steering committee and the Independent Data
9|Monitoring Committee before being submitted to dedicated regulatory authorities (depending on the country in which is
10|located a specific participating site) ahead of implementation. Study amendments to the protocol that affected the course of
11|the study and/or impacted on the study analysis are presented in an itemized fashion below (numbering and date of approval
12|correspond to the one validated by the French regulatory authorities).
13|5.1
14|Initial version of the protocol
15|The initial version of the protocol aimed to include n=916 men with de novo mCSPC treated with ADT alone as SOC. With
16|458 allocated to ADT + abiraterone (arms B and D) and 458 allocated to ADT without abiraterone (arms A and C) and a
17|total number of deaths of 406, a 4% level two-sided test of equal exponential survival would have an 80% power to detect a
18|survival difference between abiraterone-treated and abiraterone-deprived arms with a constant hazard ratio of 0.75. With the
19|same number of patients, and total number of 627 CRPC events, a 1% level two-sided test of equal exponential CRPC PFS
20|would have an 84% power to detect an improvement in PFS with a hazard ratio of 0.75. The same hypotheses were made
21|regarding the OS and PFS improvement related to the addition of prostate radiotherapy to systemic treatment.
22|5.2
23|Study amendments
24|Amendment N°14 (substantial; ethics committee approval: 07-OCT-2015)
25|Several studies1-3 published after the initial approval of PEACE-1 protocol, established the benefit of supplementing
26|androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) with docetaxel for diverse population of patients including de novo mCSPC patients,
27|the ones enrolled in PEACE-1. Therefore, the study protocol was amended to authorize the use of docetaxel as part of the
28|SOC, in patients fit to receive this treatment. Such a treatment came in effect in October 2015 at a time when 273 patients
29|had already been included. For patients unfit to receive docetaxel, the SOC remained ADT alone. The stratification factor
30|"docetaxel" (yes vs. no) was added to the randomization process. To adjust for the longer median overall survival mediated
31|by the addition of docetaxel, the median time expected in the control arm was increased by 1 year, to 5 years, and the
32|estimated follow-up duration after last patient entry until data maturity by 1 year bringing the expected study duration to 3
33|years of recruitment and 6.5 years of follow-up. The target hazard ratio and number of events (deaths) remained unchanged.
34|The IDMC pointed out that the initial sample size planned (n=916) would be underpowered with the addition of a new
35|group of patients (the docetaxel-treated) and that possible statistical interactions between the trial different components may
36|reduce the power of the study on the overall population. The submission of a revised statistical plan/sample size was
37|advised.
38|
39|Amendment N°20 (substantial; ethics committee approval: 10-AUG-2017)
40|The sample size was increased to 1168 patients (+250 patients) based on simulations incorporating a statistical quantitative
41|interaction between abiraterone and docetaxel. The clinical hypothesis was that the efficacy of abiraterone could be weaker
42|in patients treated with ADT+docetaxel compared to ADT alone as SOC. Based on the LATITUDE4 and STAMPEDE5
43|trial results (presented at the American Society of Clinical Oncology (ASCO) meeting in June 2017) demonstrating that the
44|upfront combination of abiraterone with ADT increased the overall survival of men with de novo metastatic prostate cancer
45|(PEACE-1 study indication) compared to ADT alone, it was no longer possible for ethical reasons to allow these patients to
46|be allocated to ADT alone when randomized to the SOC arm. Therefore, the protocol was amended to selectively restrict
47|accrual to the patients which could be treated with ADT+docetaxel (866 patients were already included at this time).
48|
49|Amendment N°23 (substantial; ethics committee approval: 22-MAR-2018)
50|In December 2017, two docetaxel-related deaths (one in each arm) occurred the same week at the same center. These events
51|put the trial on hold for about three months, the time for this center to be audited by both the sponsor and health authorities.
52|As both deaths were due to neutropenic fever it was decided as per the health authority requirement that the trial would be
53|restarted on the condition that an amendment was made to enforce the mandatory prescription of G-CSF along with an

6|Amendment N°32 (substantial; ethics committee approval: 13-JAN-2021)
7|Due to the Covid-19 pandemic, the submission and approval this amendment was considerably delayed. From April 2019 to
8|April 2020 changes to be made to the analysis plan were discussed with the IDMC and the Steering Committee as some
9|questions to be answered by PEACE 1 had been partially or totally solved. Specifically:
10|•
11|The efficacy of abiraterone in hormone-sensitive metastatic prostate cancer treated by ADT alone as SOC was
12|investigated by the LATITUDE study with regard to high-risk patients4, and the STAMPEDE study5
13|•
14|The efficacy of prostate radiotherapy in hormone-sensitive metastatic prostate cancer treated by ADT alone as
15|SOC was investigated by the HORRAD study6 and the STAMPEDE RT study7.
16|
17|Therefore, once authorized, this amendment allowed us to:
18|•
19|Investigate a revise co-primary objective to answer two questions of utmost interest for the medical community
20|by:
21|o
22|Assessing the efficacy of abiraterone acetate and prednisone in patients with metastatic hormone-naïve
23|prostate cancer treated by ADT and docetaxel (with or without prostate radiotherapy) in terms of overall
24|survival (OS) and radiographic progression free survival (rPFS).
25|o
26|Assessing the efficacy of prostate radiotherapy in hormone-naïve prostate cancer patients with low
27|metastatic burden (as defined in the CHAARTED trial8), regardless of the SOC received (ADT with or
28|without docetaxel, with or without abiraterone) in terms of OS and rPFS.
29|•
30|Focus on the timing of the final analyses instead of conducting intermediate analysis based on the hypotheses
31|that abiraterone in the ADT+ docetaxel population would have an efficacy and that prostate radiotherapy on the
32|population with a low metastatic burden (in accordance with the revised primary objectives) would also have an
33|efficacy.
34|•
35|Update the nature of the co-primary endpoint from PFS to radiographic PFS (rPFS): In initial protocol PFS
36|was based on rPFS and PSA progression events. However, post PEACE-1 initiation, various studies showed that
37|PSA progression had poor prognosis value as a surrogate endpoint. In contrast, rPFS was demonstrated to be a
38|valid surrogate endpoint for OS in metastatic prostate cancer and was an FDA-validated registration endpoint in
39|hormone sensitive metastatic prostate cancer settings (PEACE-1 study indication). Hence, rPFS was requalified as
40|a co-primary endpoint while PFS events already well defined and collected during the trial were used along with
41|PSA progression to characterize and evaluate CRPC-free survival as a secondary endpoint.
42|•
43|Change the distribution of the type I error between the co-primary endpoints in order to prioritize the overall
44|survival analysis. Thus, the type I error for OS was set at 4.9% instead of 4%, and at 0.1% instead of 1% for rPFS.
45|•
46|Define the testing strategy and decision rules for the fixed-sequence test in the study subpopulations to control the
47|type I error and avoid multiplicity issues. Specifically, for the abiraterone question, the choice of testing first the
48|overall population and then the ADT+docetaxel population was based on the following arguments: the trial had
49|been designed for the population of men with de novo mCSPC with a SOC comprising ADT+/- docetaxel
50|depending on the inclusion period. We felt that discarding the information provided by 40% of our study
51|population (those receiving ADT alone as SOC) was unethical. To the contrary, keeping those patients in the
52|analysis gave more power to the study (as more events were available in the overall population). The risk of being
53|stopped after testing the overall population and not being able to present data for the ADT+docetaxel population
54|was considered small, given the external efficacy data of abiraterone reported by the LATITUDE and STAMPEDE
55|studies.

answers.justification: The registry captured toxicity graded by NCI-CTCAE v4.0 before the study began (first posted Oct 8, 2013; first participant start Nov 13, 2013). The supplement describes the initial 2013 protocol and says subsequent protocol/SAP changes were made without reference to collected outcome data; the stated changes concern evolving standards, eligibility, efficacy questions, and COVID. This supports prespecification of the toxicity outcome and argues against result-driven changes. The captured documents do not provide a dated final SAP specifying the exact binary grade ≥3 contrast or the analysts' access chronology, so I judge this probably rather than definitely prespecified.
unknowns: No dated final SAP for the exact grade ≥3 binary summary or record of when the analysis team obtained unblinded safety data is captured.

answers.justification: Several severity summaries are reported: any AE, grade ≥3 AE, fatal AE, and severe-AE components. The supplement also reports both the number/proportion of participants with at least one severe AE and the severe-AE rate per 100 subject-years (with event counts and person-time). The requested binary grade ≥3 result and the related summaries are disclosed, with no evidence that only a favorable measurement was selected.

The requested safety-population proportion is reported alongside the event-rate analysis for the same docetaxel comparison, and the report states safety analyses used the safety population by treatment received. The protocol/SAP amendments were reported as unrelated to collected outcomes. I found no evidence that this particular numerical result was selected from alternative analyses because of its result.

Statistical analysis
The initial protocol in 2013 planned for a sample size of
916 patients. However, due to a change in the SOC and the
knowledge gained from the LATITUDE and STAMPEDE
trial results published in late 2017, the planned sample
size was increased to 1173 and the coprimary study aims
were revised (appendix pp 7-8). Because PEACE-1 was the
only phase 3 trial to date that could determine abiraterone
efficacy in patients with mCSPC receiving ADT plus
docetaxel as SOC, the timing of the final analyses was
based on this population (population of interest). Sample
size calculation was performed with East software (Cytel;
Cambridge, MA, USA), on the basis of the assumption
that no significant interaction would take place between
radiotherapy and abiraterone, to allow for a 2 × 2 factorial
analysis of abiraterone efficacy. For abiraterone efficacy
evaluation, the predetermined acceptable probability of a
type I error was set at 0·05, divided between the two
coprimary endpoints (0·049 for overall survival and 0·001
for
radiographic
progression-free
survival).
We
hypothesised that adding abiraterone to ADT plus
docetaxel would improve overall survival by 30% over a
median of 53 months and progression-free survival by
40% over 30 months. Hence, with 355 patients assigned to
ADT with docetaxel plus abiraterone (with or without
radiotherapy) and 355 patients assigned to ADT with
docetaxel
without
abiraterone
(with
or
without

detect an overall survival hazard ratio (HR) of 0·70 at a
two-sided α level of 0·049. With the same group allocation,
262 radiographic progression events or deaths were
predicted to have an 80% power to detect a radiographic
progression-free survival HR of 0·60 at a two-sided α level
of 0·001.
This trial had a factorial design, based on the
assumption that there would be no interaction between
abiraterone and radiotherapy. Before analysing the
various outcomes, the presence of such an interaction
for both coprimary endpoints was tested by analyses of
maximum likelihood estimates using a Cox model
adjusted for stratification factors (ECOG performance
status [0 vs 1-2], ADT type [gonadotropin-releasing
hormone agonist vs antagonist vs bilateral orchiectomy],
metastatic burden [low vs high; as defined in the
Randomisation and masking section],2 and docetaxel
[no docetaxel before amendment vs no docetaxel after
amendment vs with docetaxel after amendment]). In the
absence of a qualitative interaction (p>0·05) between
abiraterone and radiotherapy, the groups were to be
combined two by two on the basis of abiraterone
administration, regardless of radiotherapy, before se
quentially assessing abiraterone efficacy first in the
overall population and then in the ADT with docetaxel
population (assuming the significance level was reached
in first instance). As the preplanned number of pro
gression-free survival and overall survival events had
not been reached in the study population at the time
this paper was written, the efficacy of radiotherapy
remains to be analysed (appendix p 16). The coprimary
endpoint results presented here correspond to the final
planned analysis; no interim analysis was conducted.

docetaxel and abiraterone have distinct mechanisms of
action. In addition, they do not display absolute cross-
resistance, as abiraterone improves overall survival
after docetaxel treatment and docetaxel retains some
activity after abiraterone failure.30,31 Collectively, these
observations provide a rationale for the survival benefits
resulting from their combination in this trial. However,
this study did not answer whether this triple
combination yields clinical advantages over ADT plus a
second-generation androgen receptor axis inhibitor.
Indeed, at the time when this trial was conducted
(2013-18), combining ADT with such an inhibitor had
not been approved for mCSPC, thereby precluding
such a comparison within the trial. Incidentally, the
ongoing phase 3 ARASENS (NCT02799602) and
ENZAMET (NCT02446405) trials are also testing the
combined efficacy of second-generation androgen
receptor axis inhibitors (darolutamide and enzalutamide,
respectively) with ADT and docetaxel, and their
upcoming overall survival results will put the benefits
of abiraterone in perspective.
Reaching treatment synergy and preventing acquired
resistance despite tumour clonal heterogeneity are
cardinal aspects of mCSPC management that require
an optimisation of the treatment framework. In
PEACE-1, significant survival benefits were obtained
when abiraterone was added to ADT with docetaxel.
Remarkably, these benefits were observed even though
more than 80% of the SOC without abiraterone group
eventually received a second-generation androgen
receptor axis inhibitor (mostly abiraterone or enzaluta
mide) to address cancer progression. Indeed, by contrast
with previous trials, PEACE-1 investigators were allowed
to prescribe early salvage treatments to the control
group patients who showed evidence of cancer
progression. To this end, a PSA minimum value of just
0·50 ng/mL was used to define mCRPC, even in the
absence of radiographic progression. Collectively, these
observations suggest that the upfront combination
implemented in this trial is superior to the sequential
administration of these (or similar) agents as occurred
in the control group. Of note, abiraterone is approved
for metastatic prostate cancer in many countries and is
close to becoming a worldwide generic drug.

combining abiraterone with SOC improves outcomes in
men with de novo mCSPC, but it shows that combining
abiraterone with ADT and docetaxel improves overall
and radiographic progression-free survival and other

and abiraterone. Longer follow-up is required to answer
whether combining such an intensive first line systemic

5.
Amendments to the study design and statistical analysis plan
Since PEACE 1 initial protocol authorization on July 13TH, 2013, the treatment of men with de novo metastatic prostate
cancer has drastically evolved. Consequently, the study design and statistical analysis plan had to be adapted accordingly.
Changes to the study protocol and statistical analysis plan were made without any reference to the outcomes data collected
during the study. All amendments to the protocol were validated by the Steering committee and the Independent Data
Monitoring Committee before being submitted to dedicated regulatory authorities (depending on the country in which is
located a specific participating site) ahead of implementation. Study amendments to the protocol that affected the course of
the study and/or impacted on the study analysis are presented in an itemized fashion below (numbering and date of approval
correspond to the one validated by the French regulatory authorities).
5.1
Initial version of the protocol
The initial version of the protocol aimed to include n=916 men with de novo mCSPC treated with ADT alone as SOC. With
458 allocated to ADT + abiraterone (arms B and D) and 458 allocated to ADT without abiraterone (arms A and C) and a
total number of deaths of 406, a 4% level two-sided test of equal exponential survival would have an 80% power to detect a
survival difference between abiraterone-treated and abiraterone-deprived arms with a constant hazard ratio of 0.75. With the
same number of patients, and total number of 627 CRPC events, a 1% level two-sided test of equal exponential CRPC PFS
would have an 84% power to detect an improvement in PFS with a hazard ratio of 0.75. The same hypotheses were made
regarding the OS and PFS improvement related to the addition of prostate radiotherapy to systemic treatment.
5.2
Study amendments
Amendment N°14 (substantial; ethics committee approval: 07-OCT-2015)
Several studies1-3 published after the initial approval of PEACE-1 protocol, established the benefit of supplementing
androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) with docetaxel for diverse population of patients including de novo mCSPC patients,
the ones enrolled in PEACE-1. Therefore, the study protocol was amended to authorize the use of docetaxel as part of the
SOC, in patients fit to receive this treatment. Such a treatment came in effect in October 2015 at a time when 273 patients
had already been included. For patients unfit to receive docetaxel, the SOC remained ADT alone. The stratification factor
"docetaxel" (yes vs. no) was added to the randomization process. To adjust for the longer median overall survival mediated
by the addition of docetaxel, the median time expected in the control arm was increased by 1 year, to 5 years, and the
estimated follow-up duration after last patient entry until data maturity by 1 year bringing the expected study duration to 3
years of recruitment and 6.5 years of follow-up. The target hazard ratio and number of events (deaths) remained unchanged.
The IDMC pointed out that the initial sample size planned (n=916) would be underpowered with the addition of a new
group of patients (the docetaxel-treated) and that possible statistical interactions between the trial different components may
reduce the power of the study on the overall population. The submission of a revised statistical plan/sample size was
advised.

Amendment N°20 (substantial; ethics committee approval: 10-AUG-2017)
The sample size was increased to 1168 patients (+250 patients) based on simulations incorporating a statistical quantitative
interaction between abiraterone and docetaxel. The clinical hypothesis was that the efficacy of abiraterone could be weaker
in patients treated with ADT+docetaxel compared to ADT alone as SOC. Based on the LATITUDE4 and STAMPEDE5
trial results (presented at the American Society of Clinical Oncology (ASCO) meeting in June 2017) demonstrating … [excerpt; use evidence_expansions to inspect full Evidence]

additional blood test around day 6 (for early neutropenia detection) for all docetaxel-treated patients until the trial
completion. Once this amendment (N°23) was authorized on March 22, 2018 (210 patients were randomized afterwards), no
subsequent toxicity-related death was observed.
Amendment N°32 (substantial; ethics committee approval: 13-JAN-2021)
Due to the Covid-19 pandemic, the submission and approval this amendment was considerably delayed. From April 2019 to
April 2020 changes to be made to the analysis plan were discussed with the IDMC and the Steering Committee as some
questions to be answered by PEACE 1 had been partially or totally solved. Specifically:
•
The efficacy of abiraterone in hormone-sensitive metastatic prostate cancer treated by ADT alone as SOC was
investigated by the LATITUDE study with regard to high-risk patients4, and the STAMPEDE study5
•
The efficacy of prostate radiotherapy in hormone-sensitive metastatic prostate cancer treated by ADT alone as
SOC was investigated by the HORRAD study6 and the STAMPEDE RT study7.

Therefore, once authorized, this amendment allowed us to:
•
Investigate a revise co-primary objective to answer two questions of utmost interest for the medical community
by:
o
Assessing the efficacy of abiraterone acetate and prednisone in patients with metastatic hormone-naïve
prostate cancer treated by ADT and docetaxel (with or without prostate radiotherapy) in terms of overall
survival (OS) and radiographic progression free survival (rPFS).
o
Assessing the efficacy of prostate radiotherapy in hormone-naïve prostate cancer patients with low
metastatic burden (as defined in the CHAARTED trial8), regardless of the SOC received (ADT with or
without docetaxel, with or without abiraterone) in terms of OS and rPFS.
•
Focus on the timing of the final analyses instead of conducting intermediate analysis based on the hypotheses
that abiraterone in the ADT+ docetaxel population would have an efficacy and that prostate radiotherapy on the
population with a low metastatic burden (in accordance with the revised primary objectives) would also have an
efficacy.
•
Update the nature of the co-primary endpoint from PFS to radiographic PFS (rPFS): In initial protocol PFS
was based on rPFS and PSA progression events. However, post PEACE-1 initiation, various studies showed that
PSA progression had poor prognosis value as a surrogate endpoint. In contrast, rPFS was demonstrated to be a
valid surrogate endpoint for OS in metastatic prostate cancer and was an FDA-validated registration endpoint in
hormone sensitive metastatic prostate cancer settings (PEACE-1 study indication). Hence, rPFS was requalified as
a co-primary endpoint while PFS events already well defined and collected during the trial were used along with
PSA progression to characterize and evaluate CRPC-free survival as a secondary endpoint.
•
Change the distribution of the type I error between the co-primary endpoints in order to prioritize the overall
survival analysis. Thus, the type I error for OS was set at 4.9% instead of 4%, and at 0.1% instead of 1% for rPFS.
•
Define the testing strategy and decision rules for the fixed-sequence test in the study subpopulations to control the
type I error and avoid multiplicity issues. Specifically, for the abiraterone question, the choice of testing first the
overall population and then the ADT+docetaxel population was based on the following arguments: the trial had
been designed for the population of men with de novo mCSPC with a SOC comprising ADT+/- docetaxel
depending on the inclusion period. We felt that discarding the information provided by 40% of our study
population (those receiving ADT alone as SOC) was unethical. To the contrary, keeping those patients in the
analysis gave more power to the study (as more events were available in the overall population). The risk of being
stopped after testing the overall population and … [excerpt; use evidence_expansions to inspect full Evidence]

with ADT and docetaxel without abiraterone. Indeed,
docetaxel and abiraterone have distinct mechanisms of
action. In addition, they do not display absolute cross-
resistance, as abiraterone improves overall survival
after docetaxel treatment and docetaxel retains some
activity after abiraterone failure.30,31 Collectively, these
observations provide a rationale for the survival benefits
resulting from their combination in this trial. However,
this study did not answer whether this triple
combination yields clinical advantages over ADT plus a
second-generation androgen receptor axis inhibitor.
Indeed, at the time when this trial was conducted
(2013-18), combining ADT with such an inhibitor had
not been approved for mCSPC, thereby precluding
such a comparison within the trial. Incidentally, the
ongoing phase 3 ARASENS (NCT02799602) and
ENZAMET (NCT02446405) trials are also testing the
combined efficacy of second-generation androgen
receptor axis inhibitors (darolutamide and enzalutamide,
respectively) with ADT and docetaxel, and their
upcoming overall survival results will put the benefits
of abiraterone in perspective.
Reaching treatment synergy and preventing acquired
resistance despite tumour clonal heterogeneity are
cardinal aspects of mCSPC management that require
an optimisation of the treatment framework. In
PEACE-1, significant survival benefits were obtained
when abiraterone was added to ADT with docetaxel.
Remarkably, these benefits were observed even though
more than 80% of the SOC without abiraterone group
eventually received a second-generation androgen
receptor axis inhibitor (mostly abiraterone or enzaluta
mide) to address cancer progression. Indeed, by contrast
with previous trials, PEACE-1 investigators were allowed
to prescribe early salvage treatments to the control
group patients who showed evidence of cancer
progression. To this end, a PSA minimum value of just
0·50 ng/mL was used to define mCRPC, even in the
absence of radiographic progression. Collectively, these
observations suggest that the upfront combination
implemented in this trial is superior to the sequential
administration of these (or similar) agents as occurred
in the control group. Of note, abiraterone is approved
for metastatic prostate cancer in many countries and is
close to becoming a worldwide generic drug.
In conclusion, this trial not only confirms that
combining abiraterone with SOC improves outcomes in
men with de novo mCSPC, but it shows that combining
abiraterone with ADT and docetaxel improves overall
and radiographic progression-free survival and other
efficacy
endpoints
with
little
toxicity
increase.
Nonetheless, as PEACE-1 only included patients with
de novo mCSPC, it is still unclear whether this triple
therapy might benefit patients with metachronous
mCSPC. Our findings cannot directly address whether
this triplet systemic combination is superior to ADT
and abiraterone. Longer follow-up is required to answer
whether combining such an intensive first line systemic
treatment with radiotherapy to the primary tumour
might provide further clinical benefits for patients with
mCSPC. This upcoming analysis will be performed

Amendments to the study design and statistical analysis plan
Since PEACE 1 initial protocol authorization on July 13TH, 2013, the treatment of men with de novo metastatic prostate
cancer has drastically evolved. Consequently, the study design and statistical analysis plan had to be adapted accordingly.
Changes to the study protocol and statistical analysis plan were made without any reference to the outcomes data collected
during the study. All amendments to the protocol were validated by the Steering committee and the Independent Data
Monitoring Committee before being submitted to dedicated regulatory authorities (depending on the country in which is
located a specific participating site) ahead of implementation. Study amendments to the protocol that affected the course of
the study and/or impacted on the study analysis are presented in an itemized fashion below (numbering and date of approval
correspond to the one validated by the French regulatory authorities).
5.1
Initial version of the protocol
The initial version of the protocol aimed to include n=916 men with de novo mCSPC treated with ADT alone as SOC. With
458 allocated to ADT + abiraterone (arms B and D) and 458 allocated to ADT without abiraterone (arms A and C) and a
total number of deaths of 406, a 4% level two-sided test of equal exponential survival would have an 80% power to detect a
survival difference between abiraterone-treated and abiraterone-deprived arms with a constant hazard ratio of 0.75. With the
same number of patients, and total number of 627 CRPC events, a 1% level two-sided test of equal exponential CRPC PFS
would have an 84% power to detect an improvement in PFS with a hazard ratio of 0.75. The same hypotheses were made
regarding the OS and PFS improvement related to the addition of prostate radiotherapy to systemic treatment.
5.2
Study amendments
Amendment N°14 (substantial; ethics committee approval: 07-OCT-2015)
Several studies1-3 published after the initial approval of PEACE-1 protocol, established the benefit of supplementing
androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) with docetaxel for diverse population of patients including de novo mCSPC patients,
the ones enrolled in PEACE-1. Therefore, the study protocol was amended to authorize the use of docetaxel as part of the
SOC, in patients fit to receive this treatment. Such a treatment came in effect in October 2015 at a time when 273 patients
had already been included. For patients unfit to receive docetaxel, the SOC remained ADT alone. The stratification factor
"docetaxel" (yes vs. no) was added to the randomization process. To adjust for the longer median overall survival mediated
by the addition of docetaxel, the median time expected in the control arm was increased by 1 year, to 5 years, and the
estimated follow-up duration after last patient entry until data maturity by 1 year bringing the expected study duration to 3
years of recruitment and 6.5 years of follow-up. The target hazard ratio and number of events (deaths) remained unchanged.
The IDMC pointed out that the initial sample size planned (n=916) would be underpowered with the addition of a new
group of patients (the docetaxel-treated) and that possible statistical interactions between the trial different components may
reduce the power of the study on the overall population. The submission of a revised statistical plan/sample size was
advised.

Amendment N°20 (substantial; ethics committee approval: 10-AUG-2017)
The sample size was increased to 1168 patients (+250 patients) based on simulations incorporating a statistical quantitative
interaction between abiraterone and docetaxel. The clinical hypothesis was that the efficacy of abiraterone could be weaker
in patients treated with ADT+docetaxel compared to ADT alone as SOC. Based on the LATITUDE4 and STAMPEDE5

PEACE-1 is assessed and the batch is finalized. The outcome is **Grade 3 or higher adverse events**: 217/347 (63%) with abiraterone versus 181/350 (52%) without.

**Overall risk of bias: High**, driven by **measurement bias (High)**. The report described extra liver-function testing in the abiraterone arms, which could have affected detection of adverse events. The other domain ratings are deviations: Some concerns; missing outcome data: Low; randomization: Low; selection of the reported result: Low.
